title: Belrose Appraisal and Gemological Services: Points of Judgement on Engagements Running at Once
content:
# Points of Judgement: Engagements Running at Once

Each service of Belrose Appraisal and Gemological Services caps how many engagements one customer may have running under it at once, and an engagement counts as running while it stands at requested, item received, in examination, report drafted or issued. A further engagement is opened for a customer only when no engagement already recorded against the same appraisal reference stands at requested, item received, in examination, report drafted or issued. An engagement that has been delivered, has expired or has been cancelled no longer counts, so a customer may open another once one of theirs closes. Taken across all six services together, the engagements one customer may have running at once under Belrose Appraisal and Gemological Services number no more than 4.

## Which states count

| Engagement stands at | Counts as running |
|---|---|
| Requested | Yes |
| Item received | Yes |
| In examination | Yes |
| Report drafted | Yes |
| Issued | Yes |
| Delivered | No |
| Expired | No |
| Cancelled | No |

The count is taken as at the day the request is handled, from the engagement records themselves, with no look-back to engagements that have since closed.

## Points of judgement

**The customer says an earlier engagement was finished weeks ago, but its record still stands at report drafted.** The record decides. The engagement stands at a running state and counts against the customer's cap; what the customer says about it does not alter the count.

**An earlier engagement stands at issued, and the customer has not yet collected.** It counts. Issued is a running state; only delivered, expired or cancelled releases the place.

**Two engagements are recorded against the same appraisal reference, one at cancelled and one at in examination.** The one at in examination is a running engagement on that reference, so no further engagement is opened against that reference while it stands there. The cancelled one is not counted.

**A customer holds engagements at more than one service.** Each service is read against its own cap on engagements running at once, and the customer's running engagements across all services together may not exceed 4.

## Hypothetical case

Under a service whose cap on engagements running at once is a hypothetical 2, a customer holds one engagement at delivered and one at in examination. One engagement is running, the cap is 2, and no running engagement stands against the reference for the new request: a further engagement is opened. Had the delivered engagement instead stood at issued, two would be running and the cap would be met, so no further engagement is opened under that service until one of the two closes.
